info.name: Consiva - Breach Response (Agent 4)
info.description:
API contract for the Breach Response agent, covering all 30 routes defined in backend/app/api/v1/routes/incidents.py (create, list, get, classify, finding, transition, evidence x3, timeline x2, systems, analyse, impact, subjects, risk, plan, actions x2, decision, attest, failed, communications x4, report x2, close, audit). Built ENTIRELY from static code reading -- the route handlers themselves, app/agents/breach/services/*.py, app/agents/breach/schemas/incident.py, app/agents/breach/errors.py, app/agents/breach/services/lifecycle.py, and tests/test_breach_fixes_regression.py (the prior F-1..F-5 audit fixes). NOT EXECUTED LIVE against any server: the only running stack on this box is production (docker-compose.prod.yml), which is strictly off-limits, so no request in this collection has been fired. To actually run it: point baseUrl at a non-production test deployment, obtain a real bearer token (a signed-in person's JWT via Depends(get_current_user) -- this agent has no separate service-key auth path the way DSR does), and replace every placeholder id variable with a real one from that environment, in the order the folders run (later folders depend on state created by earlier ones on the SAME incident: 1 creates it, 13 queues analysis, 17 builds a plan whose actions feed 18-22's actionId, 23 drafts a communication feeding 25-26's communicationId, 27 generates the report 29's close requires).

Auth: a signed-in person's bearer JWT via Depends(get_current_user) -- every route uses the same dependency, so auth and org-scoping behave identically across all 30 routes. Nothing accepts an org_id from the caller.

Error envelope: plain `{"detail": ...}` (app/main.py's default ConsivaError/RequestValidationError handling) -- for a domain error (IncidentError subclass) `detail` is a string; for a FastAPI RequestValidationError, `detail` is the default list of {loc, msg, type} objects.

Non-disclosure: every route keyed by {incident_id} resolves it through incident_service.get_incident_or_raise, which treats an incident in another org exactly like one that does not exist -> 404 for both, never 403 (errors.py IncidentNotFoundError's own docstring states this is deliberate). Confirmed by spot-check across every {incident_id}-keyed route.

Findings surfaced while building this collection (full detail in this agent's task report; backend findings are report-only -- every backend file here belongs to one of four other active lanes, so nothing was fixed in incidents.py or app/agents/breach/** from this lane): (1) communication_service.py's approve_communication and mark_communication_sent both raise IncidentNotReadyError (409) for a communication id that does not exist or belongs to another incident, where the equivalent action-id lookups elsewhere in this agent correctly raise IncidentNotFoundError (404) -- folders 25 and 26. (2) No per-org rate limit on POST /incidents or POST /{id}/analyse, the same class of gap already fixed in Purpose Classifier and reported (not yet fixed) in DSR earlier this session -- folder 13. (3) Every free-text reason/error_detail/closure_summary field reaches the shared audit log completely unredacted, unlike evidence.detail which is scrubbed by investigation_service.redact() first -- folder 30. (4) Breach's classify route takes override_type as a bare query parameter while DSR's equivalent takes a JSON body field of the same name, and the two agents' 'unknown override value' errors return different status codes (400 here, 409 in DSR) -- folder 4. (5) Attestation text and action blocked_reason are returned verbatim through GET /{id}/actions with no redaction and no detail-reveal gate, unlike evidence -- folder 19.

CONTRACT NOTE: unlike DSR's POST /requests/{id}/classify, which takes a JSON body (ClassifyRequest{override_type}), this route's `override_type` is a bare function parameter with no Pydantic model and no explicit Query()/Body() marker (routes/incidents.py classify, `override_type: str | None = None`) -- FastAPI resolves an unmarked simple-typed parameter on a POST route as a QUERY parameter, not a body field. Two agents in the same codebase expose the 'classify with an override' operation with two different request shapes for no stated reason.

CROSS-AGENT INCONSISTENCY WORTH NOTING: DSR's equivalent ('override_type not a real request type') raises CaseNotReadyError -> 409, while Breach's raises InvalidIncidentError -> 400, for the semantically identical mistake ('the override value you supplied is not one of the valid types'). Neither is wrong in isolation (400 for a malformed value is arguably the more defensible of the two), but a client integrating with both agents cannot assume one status code for this class of error across the platform.

item.name: Happy path - queues the background job

request.description:
MUTATES STATE: if the incident is still REPORTED/VALIDATING, transitions it to INVESTIGATING, then enqueues an `incident_analysis` job on the shared agent_jobs queue (routes/incidents.py:518-542). The job runs asynchronously in a worker -- this response only reports that it was QUEUED, never progress the backend hasn't reported.

RATE-LIMITING GAP (reported, not fixed -- outside this lane's editable files): this route has NO per-org request-rate limit of any kind. grep across app/api/v1/routes/incidents.py and every app/agents/breach/services/*.py file for rate_limit/RateLimitExceededError/count_scans_since-style quota logic returns nothing. Every call enqueues a real worker job (DB reads across ROPA mappings and all of an incident's evidence), so a caller looping on this endpoint -- or on POST /incidents itself, which has the identical gap -- can flood the job queue with no backend check at all. Purpose Classifier (consent_agent.py:180-187, RateLimitExceededError, count_scans_since-based hourly quota) and the equivalent DSR gap (reported earlier this session, not yet fixed) are the two other instances of exactly this class of gap on this platform; Breach is the third and has neither endpoint protected. Suggested fix location: a per-org count against incident_cases created in the last hour before create_incident commits (incidents.py:253-283), and a similar count against queued incident_analysis jobs before start_analysis enqueues another one (incidents.py:518-542).

CROSS-CUTTING AUDIT FINDING (this agent's own lane, spot-checked every audit_service.record(...) call site across incident_service.py, investigation_service.py, response_service.py, communication_service.py and sla_service.py): no call passes a raw evidence.detail dict or a communication body -- both are deliberately excluded from every after={...} payload in this codebase. BUT every free-text `reason`/`error_detail`/`closure_summary` field DOES reach the audit log completely unredacted: incident_service.py transition() (`after={'error_detail': error_detail, **(detail or {})}`, ~line 206-209) and set_finding() (`after={field: confidence, 'reason': reason}`, ~line 314), response_service.py decide_action() (`after={..., 'reason': reason, ...}`, ~line 433-437), and communication_service.py approve_communication() (`after={..., 'reason': reason}`, ~line 439-440) all write a human-typed free-text field straight into the shared audit log with none of investigation_service.redact()'s credential-pattern scrubbing applied. A reviewer who pastes 'disabled using the temp password Xk29!af' into any approval/rejection/finding/closure reason field writes that credential into the permanent audit trail. Suggested fix (outside this lane's editable files): route every free-text reason/detail value through investigation_service.redact_text() before it reaches audit_service.record's after= payload, in incident_service.py, response_service.py and communication_service.py.
